chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Sukūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

ʿAlī عليه السلام would not impose liability for what grazing animals damaged during the day, and he would say: “The owner of the crop is responsible for protecting his crop.” But he would impose liability for what grazing animals damaged at night.

key_terms.صَاحِبِ الزَّرْعِ: the owner of the cultivated crop
key_terms.يُضَمِّنُ: to hold legally liable for compensation

ai.seo_question: Is the owner of animals liable for crop damage caused by them during the day or at night in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling attributed to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding damage caused by animals to crops. It distinguishes between daytime and nighttime damage, placing responsibility on the crop owner by day and imposing liability for animal-caused damage by night.
